propositions: The false_accept computation at parity.py:81 counts not-blocked safe items instead of blocked safe items, inverting the error rate (specificity vs its complement)

Both consumption sites (parity.py:125 non-inferiority check and parity.py:252 ceiling against 0.10) treat false_accept as a lower-is-better error rate, but the inverted computation makes correct candidates fail and perfect runs score 1.0 instead of 0.0
The corrected computation must count safe items that WERE blocked (decision == 'block'), aligning with eval.py:399's settled definition of false_accept as wrongly-fired / must-not-fire

A candidate with lower false-firing rate than baseline (fewer safe items blocked) must pass the non-inferiority check; under the pre-fix metric it failed with 'false-accept rose' on the live frontier slot despite improved accuracy

The fidelity_spot_eval fixture contradictorily labelled CONFLICT blocks as 'advisory' (safe, must-not-block) while comments stated they must be blocked, survivable only because the inverted metric always scored them 0.0
